hook: Free cancer drugs allegedly sold to *15,000+* patients, Telangana too
hook_b: Free cancer drugs allegedly sold to *15,000+* patients, Telangana too
tldr: A Karnataka SIT says a racket diverted free cancer medicines from the Karnataka government and companies and sold them at high prices in six states, including Telangana.

beats.what: The accused allegedly hid a scheme where buying two injections worth about Rs 5 lakh got a third free, and sold the free dose too.
beats.why: It allegedly ran through private hospitals and pharmacy outlets, mainly in South India.
beats.care: Cancer patients' families: ask your hospital in writing about free-dose schemes before paying.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: The alleged kingpin has been taken into Delhi Police custody in a separate Rs 2 crore cheating case.

cards.q: Should hospitals have to display free-drug schemes to patients?

qs: How can patients check whether a drug they paid for was meant to be free?

facts.t: Two injections cost about *Rs 5 lakh*; a third was supposed to be free.

steps.e: Free doses from govt and firms diverted
Free dose sold at market price
Unused doses bought back cheap, resold

viz.verdict: Patients allegedly paid for medicine meant to be free
AP, Karnataka, Kerala, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Himachal

watch: The SIT is working out how many injections were diverted and the money trail.

sources.name: Telangana Today (IANS)
sources.title: Free cancer medicines allegedly sold at high prices, over 15,000 patients cheated across six states including Telangana, Andhra

fact: Free cancer medicines were allegedly sold to over *15,000* patients in six states
twist: When a patient died, the gang allegedly bought back unused injections cheap and resold them at full price.
